posts.title: 避免 worktree 残留的最佳策略是在 AGENTS.md 里面添加规则，要求 worktree 不遗留，让 Agent 自己去清理。 https://t.co/8PJDdgTE5u > worktree 不遗留：在 worktree（含 subagent 的 .claude/worktrees/agent-*）里做的任务，完成时必须删除该 worktree 及其分支。它专用的 cargo target 目录一并删掉。删除前二选一：合并进 main；或不合并时先把未提交改动提交到该分支，打 archive/<worktree 名> tag 存档，再 git worktree remove + git branch -D。编排 subagent 的会话负责收尾它派生的 worktree。确需保留的（待用户裁决、有冲突待解）在最终回复里点名路径与原因，不得默默留下。

SK hynix’s 3Q26 Revenue Surpasses ₩100T as Operating Margin Hits Record 80% SK hynix reported revenue of ₩104.6155T in 3Q26, up 32% QoQ and 328% YoY, marking the first time quarterly revenue has exceeded ₩100T. Operating profit reached ₩83.3338T, up 632% YoY, while operating margin climbed to a record 80%. SK hynix attributed its strong performance primarily to high-value products, including HBM, server DDR5, and enterprise SSDs (eSSDs). DRAM ASPs rose nearly 30% QoQ, with bit shipments increasing by approximately 10%, while NAND Flash prices climbed by more than 20%. The company noted that AI infrastructure demand is expanding beyond a handful of major CSPs to mainstream enterprises and national-level initiatives. Over the medium to long term, demand is also expected to extend into physical AI applications such as autonomous vehicles and robotics. However, advanced process complexity and lengthy fab construction timelines will constrain supply growth, and SK hynix expects structural memory shortages to persist through 2030. However, investors and stakeholders raised concerns as the listing would reduce SK hynix’s ownership of Solidigm and dilute the subsidiary’s contribution to the parent company’s earnings by around 10%. #TrendForce notes that Solidigm’s production is concentrated on 1XXL and 2XXL NAND nodes, with a focus on high-capacity QLC products. While the company has benefited from AI-driven supply shortages and price increases, its future performance could become more volatile as #YMTC expands production and Solidigm faces limited competitive advantages in high-end, high-speed SSDs. TrendForce believes SK hynix’s decision to postpone the IPO is primarily intended to avoid a potential drag on the parent company’s valuation should Solidigm’s performance weaken after listing. Keeping Solidigm within the group also allows SK hynix to retain the subsidiary’s current earnings contributions.

My thoughts on the Israeli elections: This result matters more for the Iran war than I first assumed. Exit polls show Netanyahu’s bloc falling from 68 to roughly 50 seats. Neither bloc reaches 61, and the Arab parties, at 17–18 seats, are effectively kingmakers. Netanyahu is likely on his way out, though nothing is final until a coalition is formed, and that process realistically takes six to ten weeks, with a repeat election a real possibility. Until then, Netanyahu stays on as caretaker prime minister with formal war powers. There’s no leadership vacuum, but his political room has collapsed. A discretionary escalation against Iran now would be self-defeating: he has just lost his majority, and a strike seen as a survival tactic would hand the opposition exactly the justification it needs to close ranks, including accepting Arab-party support, and remove him. The Attorney General and President Herzog add institutional friction on top. In practice, Israeli-initiated escalation is off the table until a new government forms, which will be well after the US midterms on November The American side was already closed before the midterms, assuming this is true, since Trump publicly pledge

Cliff Sosin on the limits of intelligence: "Superintelligence arrived. You probably didn't notice, because it turned out to be kind of incremental. I think we overrated intelligence, or misread what it is. We hold a thin scatter of facts about the world, and intelligence or reasoning is whatever fills the space between them. Where the space between the facts behaves well, this is close to godlike. Most of what matters doesn't behave like that. The universe is mostly the emergent behavior of complex systems. Stir cream into coffee. Watch a storm build out of nothing but atmospheric temperature differences and water vapor. You have to run the thing. The takeoff story assumed the limit was thinking. It isn't. The limit is contact with reality. A smarter reasoner fills the gaps between known facts in simple areas faster and better, but it doesn’t produce new facts. An AI will hand you a genuinely clever design for a jet turbine blade. It might be far more likely to work than anything your engineers came up with. It'll still probably fail, because that’s the base rate at the edge of what anyone knows. The only way to find out is to build the blade and try to break it. That's the real li

If intelligence becomes cheap and ubiquitous, what you want to own are the complements to intelligence. The complements are data, attention, love, physical proximity, scale, regulatory capture. Let's talk about Meta. They have $250 billion of revenue, and they spend $250 billion a year. The question you might ask is, what do they spend it on? A really reductionist view is that they spend it all on intelligence. They're buying data centers. They're literally buying inference. They're paying really smart people to write algorithms. They're writing code. That's just intelligence. If you think forward with the fact that the price of intelligence is falling by a factor of a hundred or something over the next five years, their costs kind of go away.
